issues.description: StockIngredient constructor parameters are inconsistent with the UML/specification. The problem statement UML specifies `StockIngredient(String, int, int)`, and the reference solution implements a 3-parameter constructor accordingly. However, the template defines only `StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation)`, so students cannot instantiate StockIngredient as required without changing the provided API.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to provide `public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity)` matching the UML. If strict validation is desired, keep it internally or as an overloaded constructor, but ensure the 3-parameter constructor exists and is the primary expected API.

issues.description: SealSaloon `stock` is inconsistent between UML and textual requirements. The UML shows `stock` as an instance association (implying a per-saloon Stock), while the text explicitly requires `stock` to be static/shared across all SealSaloon instances. The solution follows the text by declaring `private static final Stock stock = new Stock();`, which contradicts the UML and can confuse students about whether stock is shared or per instance.
issues.suggestedFix: Make UML and text consistent: either update the UML to explicitly indicate `stock` is static/shared, or remove the static requirement from the text and implement `stock` as a per-instance `final Stock` field.
